semantic_notes: Decision context introduces no quantitative state delta.
Preserves the counterfactual opportunity cost of preparing her own taxes.
The stated increase is retained as a comparison with the self-tax alternative.
assumptions: Interprets "earned $15 more" as earning $15 more under the accountant alternative than under the self-tax alternative.

semantic_notes: Names and returns the requested hiring cost.
assumptions: Assumes the accountant alternative's $15 earnings advantage is net of the accountant's fee, so the fee equals avoided self-tax earnings loss minus that advantage.

semantic_notes: Peter's initial sock count is distinguished from his count after donating socks.

semantic_notes: Preserves Peter's sock counts before and after the donation.
The requested aggregate includes both people's current socks and dishes.
assumptions: Assumes Jack's collected quantities are his current quantities and that Peter gave away socks only, leaving his dishes unchanged.

semantic_notes: Narrative setup introduces no quantitative state delta.
Each requested count remains attached to its laboratory-item type.
The two gathering deviations are represented independently.
assumptions: Interprets the elliptical phrase after the comma as saying Igor gathered two more Petri dishes than requested.

semantic_notes: The outage duration is retained separately from the beaker-loss relation.
assumptions: Assumes beakers not lost on the way reached the lab bench.

The beakers remaining on the bench are isolated from the total before computing the loss.
assumptions: Assumes all gathered test tubes and Petri dishes reached the bench and that only beakers were lost in transit.

Distinguishes per-shelf capacity from the combined capacity of the two middle shelves.

assumptions: Interprets "a middle shelf" as either middle shelf because both have the stated capacity.

semantic_notes: Preserves the qualitative fewer-than relation through the forward-referenced difference requested later.
assumptions: Treats the later-requested top-to-bottom capacity difference as the amount by which the top shelf holds fewer books.

semantic_notes: Exact fit grounds each identical bookcase's capacity and thereby the top-shelf capacity.
assumptions: Assumes the two new bookcases have the same shelf layout and capacities and that "just enough" means their combined capacity equals 110 books.

Separates durations and distances by travel mode before forming the total distance to the destination.
assumptions: Assumes the full ten-hour trip consisted only of driving and hiking and that the distances traveled by both modes add along one route to the vacation spot.
